shortName: Northwestern University The Feinberg School of Medicine
additionalCoursework: Additional coursework in genetics, public health, the humanities and the social sciences (e.g., psychology, sociology, ethics) is recommended.

medSchoolStudLife.diversity: FSM is deeply committed to advancing healthcare for all. We strive to create a setting that allows students to influence the learning environment, challenge faculty and administrators, and explore and celebrate different backgrounds. Within our MD Program, we prioritize the importance of cultural humility in our training. Supported by our various clinical settings, we impart on our students that comprehensive care requires serving the individual patient’s unique needs, abilities, values, and challenges.  Our Office of Health Equity supports a number of programs for all students to explore, to become engaged in, and to develop. We also have initiatives to help students find community and mentoring so they can thrive at Feinberg.  For more info, please visit this page: https://www.feinberg.northwestern.edu/health-equity/index.html
medSchoolStudLife.leaveOfAbsence: Leaves are approved for various personal or academic reasons including research or pursuit of a related degree.  Students are required to complete the MD degree within six years of matriculation unless approved by the Student Promotions Committee.
medSchoolStudLife.organizationActivities: Feinberg students organize themselves into an amazing array of groups based on interests in academic disciplines, artistic pursuits, advocacy for disadvantaged groups, volunteering in free clinics and tutoring, athletics, and much more. Students take advantage of Feinberg's location in downtown Chicago to experience the cultural opportunities of a world-class city. Feinberg has dozens of active student groups that focus on such themes as identity, career goals, community involvement, performing arts, and service give students the opportunity to get involved outside the classroom. From In Vivo to the Northwestern Medical Orchestra, the many medical specialty interest groups, and other organizations, these activities serve as an outlet for our students’ interests. For more information, please visit this page: https://www.feinberg.northwestern.edu/md-education/student-support/student-groups.html
medSchoolStudLife.setting: Located in the Streeterville neighborhood of downtown Chicago, the medical school is adjacent to beautiful Lake Michigan and within easy walking distance of apartments, museums, restaurants, athletic facilities, and retailers. Public and university transportation (CTA and Intercampus Shuttles) makes Chicago's 77 neighborhoods and cultural opportunities readily accessible. Streeterville is only one neighborhood in this exciting city full of unique pockets that reflect the many cultures that live here. No matter your extracurricular interests – sports, art, music, theater, fitness, food – there are endless options. For more information, please visit this page: https://www.feinberg.northwestern.edu/admissions/why-northwestern/chicago.html
medSchoolStudLife.housing: Most students live in high rise apartments near the medical center, in the Streeterville and Gold Coast neighborhoods, and excellent public transportation (students are issued a Ventra U-Pass) makes commuting from city neighborhoods or Chicago's suburbs feasible. For more information, please visit this page: https://www.feinberg.northwestern.edu/admissions/faq/campus-housing-faq.html
medSchoolStudLife.supportSystems: Northwestern University and the Feinberg School of Medicine are deeply committed to creating an inclusive campus setting for all students.  Specific initiatives to educate and engage the Feinberg community include LGBTQ Safe Space training, the LGBTQ+ Alliance, the OUT Network Chicago, and access to additional Northwestern and Chicago community support resources.  The Feinberg community works to ensure a welcoming and supportive environment.  For more information, please visit this page: https://www.feinberg.northwestern.edu/health-equity/resources-training/index.html
medSchoolStudLife.supportSystemsForDisabilities: AccessibleNU (ANU) is responsible for the academic and on-campus housing accommodation determination and coordination process for students with disabilities. Northwestern University recognizes disability as an essential aspect of our campus, and as such, we actively collaborate with faculty, staff, and students to achieve access goals. Accommodations can be made for each phase of medical education. Medical students with disabilities are encouraged to register with ANU as early as possible in their medical education. Accommodations are arranged on a case-by-case basis for all types of exams and clinical rotations in collaboration with the Feinberg School of Medicine.  For more information, please visit this page: https://www.northwestern.edu/accessiblenu/
medSchoolStudLife.wellnessPrograms: At Northwestern University Feinberg School of Medicine, we believe that wellness and self-care are essential to academic success and a rewarding career. Helping our students cultivate physical, emotional, and spiritual wellness helps them develop the skills they need to approach their education and future careers with resilience, balance and satisfaction. Find more information about wellness resources here: https://www.feinberg.northwestern.edu/md-education/current-students/wellness/index.html
medSchoolStudLife.campusCulture: Feinberg encourages unique perspectives from within our academic community. We believe this approach provides a rich environment for education and leads to groundbreaking scientific discovery. Mentoring is an important part of the Feinberg experience. Feinberg students will have multiple faculty mentors throughout their four years. Through our college structure each student is assigned to a college headed by a faculty mentor. Under their leadership, ~18 students develop trust and help one another learn & adapt to the culture of medicine. Through the Area of Scholarly Concentration, students are assigned a faculty advisor, along with self-identifying an AOSC faculty research mentor. Through the ECMH program, a four-year clinical faculty preceptor will guide students' clinical skills development.
medSchoolStudLife.transportationAdditionalInfo:
The campus is centrally located in downtown Chicago and easy to get to by public transportation, such as buses and elevated trains (widely referred to as “the L”). The public Chicago Transit Authority (CTA) system can get you nearly anywhere, including both Midway and O’Hare airports.

Shortly after matriculation, FSM students are issued a Ventra U-Pass, a discounted student fare card for unlimited rides on CTA trains and buses.

medSchoolCurriculum.dressCode: Appropriate deportment and dress are expected of students as they engage with patients and clinical colleagues.
medSchoolCurriculum.tutoringPrograms: FSM offers many types of support: study skills resources & workshops, tutoring (senior students and faculty), drop-in office hours with Deans, financial planning, career advising, & wellness programs.
medSchoolCurriculum.patientInteraction: Early clinical experiences begin the first week of medical school. Learn more here: https://www.feinberg.northwestern.edu/md-education/curriculum/components/elements/clinical-medicine.html
medSchoolCurriculum.instructionStyle: Combination of lecture, small groups, active learning, multimodal learning, and hands-on clinical experiences.
medSchoolCurriculum.clinicalRotations: Clinical skills acquisition begins in the first week.  Full-time clinical clerkships begin third year. Learn more here: https://www.feinberg.northwestern.edu/md-education/curriculum/phases/index.html
medSchoolCurriculum.prematriculationProgram: Through the Office of Health Equity, accepted students matriculating at FSM can participate in a summer experience focused on research & community partnership in an area of their choosing.
medSchoolCurriculum.lectureAttendance: Our curriculum enables both self-directed as well as guided learning. Students engage with didactic material in different ways. Video recordings will be made of non-required classroom sessions.
medSchoolCurriculum.curricularHighlights: The FSM curriculum provides a student-centered environment where active learners use their questions as the starting point for inquiry. All 4 years of instruction include components from the 4 curricular elements (Science in Medicine, Clinical Medicine, Health & Society, and Professional Development) and the 5 threads that run through the curriculum (Healthcare Quality & Patient Safety, Medical Decision Making & Diagnostic Testing, Interprofessional Education, Health Equity & Advocacy, and Digital Health & Data Science). Phase 1 features an integrated, organ-system based approach in Science in Medicine.  Problem Based Learning and Team Based Learning contextualize the concepts developed in lectures and laboratory sessions. FSM's curriculum is informed by 9 organizing principles: Adaptive & Personalized, Community Engagement & Service Learning, Competency-Based, Continuity, Evidence-Based, Safe & Healthy, Inquiry-Driven, Integrated, and Professional Development.
medSchoolCurriculum.primaryCarePrograms: At the beginning of the first year, students join an Education Centered Medical Home (ECMH) which serves as their longitudinal clinical site throughout their time at Feinberg. The ECMH is an innovative program in which one preceptor and a group of students from all four years work as a team to care for patients in a primary care setting. Students attend ECMH for one half-day every other week and gradually take on more responsibility as their skills grow.  This clinical placement fosters professional development, skill acquisition and informs everything the student is learning, from basic science to ethics to health economics and the principles of quality and safety.  In essence, the ECMH creates "the need to know" and sparks the desire for self-directed, lifelong learning in the service of patients. This longitudinal continuity also allows students to develop deeper relationships and more meaningful collaborations.
medSchoolCurriculum.researchPrograms: Feinberg offers several combined degree programs with a major emphasis on research (MD-PhD, MD-MPH, MD-MBA, and MD-MA in Medical Humanities and Bioethics).  In addition, all students are encouraged to explore research interests.  Students participating in the Area of Scholarly Concentration will engage in a highly-mentored research project across all three phases of the curriculum. Complementing the AOSC curriculum and project, our competitive Research Intensive Scholarly Emphasis (RISE) program provides the opportunity for students (MD and MD/MPH) to spend an extra, funded year of mentored research during their training. Feinberg offers a broad range of research options including basic, translational, clinical, epidemiologic, educational, patient safety and health care policy. Learn more here: https://www.feinberg.northwestern.edu/md-education/curriculum/components/learning-strategies/student-research/index.html
medSchoolCurriculum.academicSystemText: Please visit our site for further information about the MD curriculum: https://www.feinberg.northwestern.edu/md-education/curriculum/index.html
medSchoolCurriculum.communityServiceText: Students join an Education Centered Medical Home: https://www.feinberg.northwestern.edu/md-education/curriculum/components/learning-strategies/education-centered-medical-home/
medSchoolCurriculum.researchThesisText: Students complete a highly mentored longitudinal research project over their 4 years in their Area of Scholarly Concentration (AOSC).
medSchoolCurriculum.affiliatedHospitals: FSM is affiliated with Northwestern Medicine, Prentice Women's, Lurie Children's, the Shirley Ryan AbilityLab, Stroger Cook County, and the Jesse Brown Veterans Administration Hospitals.
medSchoolCurriculum.gradingSystem: Pass/Pass After Remediation in Phase 1 and then Honor/High Pass/Pass in the clerkships.

medSchoolInformation.generalInformation: Northwestern University's Feinberg School of Medicine (FSM), founded in 1859, continues to educate today's students at a premier medical school and outstanding hospitals: Northwestern Memorial, Lurie Children's, Prentice Women's, Shirley Ryan AbilityLab, Stroger Cook County, and the Jesse Brown VA Medical Center. Our location gives students access to our top-rated clinical affiliates as well as to the city of Chicago’s vibrant cultural landscape.  At Feinberg, our ultimate goal is educating future leaders in medicine. To accomplish this, we value excellence in all arenas, from clinical care to research. Our students not only receive hands-on clinical experience from day one, they also use state-of-the-art facilities like our simulation center, volunteer in community clinics, pursue global health opportunities, and have basic science, translational and clinical research options as well as the opportunity to engage the cultural life of Chicago and work with its population.
medSchoolInformation.missionStatement:
Our mission is to impact the practice of medicine through discovery and education to improve human health. Our vision is to achieve this mission through continuous quality improvement.

The pursuit of excellence requires a learning organization grounded in leadership, innovation, and compassionate care that can translate new knowledge into better human health. These attributes are interwoven by professionalism dedicated to teamwork, collegiality, and social and intellectual curiosity. Such values promote the best interests of medicine and further strengthen our social contract with the community we serve.

medSchoolApplication.amcasLettersText: Nontraditional applicants/students are generally defined as those who have taken two or more years off between undergraduate studies and matriculation to medical school. If you submit individual letters, you will need to submit a total of three separate letters to meet Feinberg’s letters requirement. For nontraditional applicants, letters may be procured from any combination of the following sources: science or non-science faculty members; supervisors from research, clinical shadowing, volunteer, or work experiences.
medSchoolApplication.letterGuidance:
Committee/Composite/Advisor Letter: A comprehensive and detailed letter authored by a pre-health committee or pre-health adviser and intended to represent your institution’s evaluation of you. If your institution writes a committee letter WITH individual letters included, this will be acceptable, and they will all be considered during the review of your application.  If your institution writes a brief committee letter WITHOUT individual letters included, you will need to send at least two additional individual letters.

Individual Letters: a total of three separate letters meets Feinberg’s requirement. At least one letter should come from a science faculty member. The other two letters may come from a variety of sources, preferably faculty members (science or non-science) or a research supervisor, but may also include a long-term employer. 

https://www.feinberg.northwestern.edu/admissions/how-to-apply/requirements.html
medSchoolApplication.typicalInterviewDay: The virtual interview day consists of an orientation, interviews with faculty members and senior medical students, along with conversations with our 1st and 2nd-year medical students. The details for the interview day will be provided when interview invitations are sent.
medSchoolApplication.interviewFormat: Combination of interviews with full-time faculty and a senior medical student.
medSchoolApplication.videoInterview: Cycle 2027 interviews will be conducted virtually.
medSchoolApplication.secApplSentTo: All applicants with an MCAT score of 500 or higher.
medSchoolApplication.acceptInternationalApplInformation: International students are ineligible for most federal assistance programs, and thus must secure private funding through a participating lender with a US-based co-signer.
medSchoolApplication.dacaDetail: Students with DACA status are ineligible for most federal assistance programs, and thus must secure private funding through a participating lender with a US-based co-signer.
medSchoolApplication.additionalInfo:
Up-to-date Feinberg Admissions Policies and Procedures can be found on our site: https://www.feinberg.northwestern.edu/admissions/

An AMCAS Application is required for all individuals applying to the MD or MD/PhD program at Feinberg.  Once Feinberg receives the AMCAS Application, applicants with an MCAT score of 500 or higher will be asked to complete and submit a Feinberg-specific Secondary Application.  After all application materials have been received, each file is comprehensively reviewed by the Executive Committee on Admissions, and interview offers are extended to applicants on an ongoing, rolling basis from August through January each cycle.  Interviews are required.  Feinberg operates on a modified rolling admissions process that utilizes a batched approach to sending acceptances, with a small subset of early acceptances released during the interview season and the majority of the final decisions released after the interview season.
medSchoolApplication.mcatScoresAdditionalInfo: More weight is placed on most recent performance(s) and trend in performances.
medSchoolApplication.mcatScreenAdditionalInfo: All applicants with an MCAT score of 500 or higher will receive a secondary application invitation. We encourage our prospective applicants to explore our Entering Class Profile https://www.feinberg.northwestern.edu/admissions/about/entering-class-profile.html and review the Characteristics of a Successful Candidate https://www.feinberg.northwestern.edu/admissions/how-to-apply/candidate-characteristics.html to learn more about our Feinberg matriculants.
medSchoolApplication.gpaScreenAdditionalInfo: Although we don’t have a minimum GPA requirement, we encourage our prospective applicants to explore our Entering Class Profile https://www.feinberg.northwestern.edu/admissions/about/entering-class-profile.html and review the Characteristics of a Successful Candidate https://www.feinberg.northwestern.edu/admissions/how-to-apply/candidate-characteristics.html to learn more about our Feinberg matriculants.
medSchoolApplication.minUndergradGpaInfo: All post-baccalaureate and post-graduate work is given consideration in the comprehensive review process.
medSchoolApplication.minCreditHourInfo: All post-baccalaureate and post-graduate work is given consideration in the comprehensive review process.
medSchoolApplication.courseworkAcceptanceInfo: Coursework completed at a junior or community college will be included in our holistic review. We recommend that the required pre-med courses be completed at a four-year college or university.
medSchoolApplication.letterOfIntentAdditionalInfo: Applicants may utilize the 'Document Upload' section of the FSM application portal to upload letters of intent/interest or application updates at any point throughout the cycle. They will then be immediately available as part of their applicant file to be reviewed by the FSM Executive Committee on Admissions (ECOA).
medSchoolApplication.technicalStandardInfo:
Applicants are asked to evaluate themselves according to the technical standards established by the faculty before matriculation and at various points throughout the curriculum. These standards include observation and communication skills, reasoning abilities and motor skills necessary for the performance of laboratory tests and diagnostic procedures.

Please visit the website below for description of technical standards the faculty deems necessary for students to matriculate, remain in good standing and ultimately achieve all competencies necessary for graduation with the MD degree. FSM requires applicants to confirm their ability to comply with these standards, with or without reasonable accommodation, as a condition of admission to the MD program. FSM is committed to the full and equitable inclusion of qualified learners with disabilities. Students with disabilities should contact Accessible NU for information on how to request accommodations.

medSchoolFinancial.financialAid: Financial considerations do not influence admissions decisions. We make every effort to ensure that accepted students receive a competitive financial aid package covering the cost of attendance. Financial aid may include support through merit scholarships, need-based grants, and loans. All students are offered individual financial management counseling. Learn more here: https://www.feinberg.northwestern.edu/admissions/how-to-apply/tuition-financial-aid.html

medSchoolSelection.premedReqRec:
We require two years of chemistry (one year of inorganic or its equivalent, and either one year of organic or one semester of organic and one semester of biochemistry), a year each of general biology and physics.  We suggest that students also take courses in the social sciences, humanities and statistics in order to broaden their preparation for medical studies.

Prospective students are encouraged to pursue a balanced education with a major in an area of interest. No preferences is given to those who have majored in the sciences over those who have pursued the humanities. Feinberg strives to recruit a student body with broad academic interests and encourages applications from students who have majored outside the traditional premedical disciplines of biology and chemistry, including the other sciences, engineering, the humanities and social sciences.
medSchoolSelection.oldestPrereqDate: There is no age limit on coursework completed. If a student has taken the pre-med coursework a while ago, they may want to retake the courses in order to prepare for the MCAT and medical school.
medSchoolSelection.selectionFactors: Our Committee on Admissions looks for evidence of academic excellence, mature motivation for a career in medicine, altruism, and character. A premium is placed on the breadth and depth of academic and life experiences, as well as clinical and research exposure. Applicants should be liberally educated learners whose studies have gone beyond the conventional premedical courses. We do not discriminate based on race, religion, national origin, gender, gender identity, sexual orientation, age, or disability. The Illinois Medical School Matriculant Criminal History Records Act requires each entering medical student to submit to a criminal history records check before matriculation.  Students entering Feinberg must also submit to a required drug screening before matriculating at the school.
medSchoolSelection.preMedShadowText: While Feinberg does not have a mandatory requirement of shadowing doctors to be considered for admission, applicants should have exposure to the healthcare field so they can explore their motivation and fit for pursuing a medical degree. Our students bring a variety of medicine-related experiences and exposures to Feinberg including clinical and hospital volunteering, medical scribing, EMT training/practice, and clinical research.
